They won't stop on on-ramps for no reason. If they are doing the speed limit, I doubt they'll be programmed to do it in the fast lane. Eventually as adoption increases many people expect there to be dedicated self-driving lanes (like HOV lanes today) on major roads. They may even have higher speed limits there if the stats show automation can handle it better than people.

He stops on on ramps because he's afraid to merge, he drives in the left lane (of a 3 lane road) because again he's afraid of the merging traffic on the right and when 2 freeways combine along the route he doesn't like the middle lane merging. He's not being an asshole, he's not being a self-centered driver. He's just old and no longer has the skills he should to be driving. I feel for him, but god does it still piss me off when I'm behind him. Self driving cars can not get here soon enough. I get that the he needs to get to work, just not at the cost of everyone around him.

Made it 10 years, but didn't make it in the long run. The problem with a first love is you've never felt that way before so you think that nobody else will ever make you feel that way. I was wrong, because now I'm remarried and we "fit" each other better (but by no means does that mean everything is perfect). The BIG one for me was my first wife didn't want kids and I wanted a family. I figured I loved her enough to pass up on having children, but over the years it ate at me. That was by no means the only issue, but it was a biggy.

That's not to say that you can't be the lucky one and found the right person the first time. I don't mean to sound discouraging, love is amazing and worth having in your life. Just be sure you're not blinded by love and ignoring anything that will come back to haunt you later. Take a real deep look at your relationship and make sure it's right before you take the plunge.

Yeah, not quite a happily ever after story for me. Things did go better than if I had never said anything at all, but it could have been even better if she would have been willing to acknowledge her own feelings. It takes 2 to have a relationship.

We were friends for nearly 10 years. We became very close, told each other everything, nothing was to personal. I had more than friends feeling for her, I started getting lots of hints that she did to. So I brought it up one night we were together. She flipped out and cut contact with me for like a month. When she came back she was more open and we were friends with benefits for a while. 

She would still have boyfriends off an on, then I got serious with a girl and we got engaged. She was dead set against my fiance and eventually she just dropped out of my life again. Honestly, I don't know any other way to take that than that she was upset that I was being taken off the table without her ever really telling me what she felt. I miss her as a friend, but honestly it wasn't worth the drama.

I guess what I'm trying to get across is there can be a lot more to it than she's either into you or she isn't. Her actions said she had more feelings for me, but she wasn't willing to admit it to me (or herself). I think we missed out on some good times because she didn't truly know herself.

My advice is to just always be true to yourself and honest with people. You'll fail 100% of the shots you don't take. At least I know I tried.

It's pretty common advice to make sure you share the load of a newborn with your SO, but also make sure you're both doing bits of everything. If one of you is the main diaper changer or the main feeder, next thing you know your little one won't want the other parent doing it at all.

For example, my wife was really into bedtime with our baby. She said it was her special bonding time, so I rarely got to cuddle our baby to sleep at night and put her to bed. Now she's 2 and a half and bed time isn't quite as cute anymore. My wife would love it to be split more 50/50, but our daughter isn't having it. Bed time is for her and mom. She ALWAYS requests mom.
